en.name: Chia seeds
en.summary: Chia seeds keep 18 months in a sealed jar in a cool dry cupboard. They are oily but unusually stable — the whole seed's hull protects the fat inside, which is why they outlast most ground seeds by a long way.
en.pantry: A sealed jar in a cool, dark, dry cupboard, 18 months. Chia is about a third oil and that oil is highly unsaturated, which would normally make it fragile; what protects it is the intact hull of the whole seed and the natural antioxidants in it. Keep them whole for as long as possible — once you grind chia, the protection is gone and it behaves like any other ground seed, going stale within weeks rather than months. Keep the jar away from the hob and out of direct sun, and keep it dry: chia absorbs many times its weight in water and a damp spoon will turn the surface into gel.
en.fridge: Refrigeration is not necessary for whole chia seeds and the cupboard figure already covers a year and a half. It does no harm in a very hot kitchen, but the fridge is humid, and chia is one of the most hygroscopic things you can put in it — a badly sealed jar will gel at the edges and then clump solid. If you do refrigerate them, use a gasket jar and let it come back to room temperature before opening it so condensation forms on the glass rather than on the seeds.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for chia seeds and there is very little to gain from freezing whole ones. Ground chia is a different matter: if you grind a batch, the freezer is the sensible place for it, sealed hard and used straight from frozen. As always with a dry good, let the container come back to room temperature before you open it, or the condensation will start the gelling you are trying to avoid.
spoilage: A bitter, fishy or paint-like smell from the oil — most likely in ground chia.
Seeds clumped or gelled together, meaning moisture has got in.
A musty smell or visible mould in a jar that got damp.
Insects or webbing in the container.
tips: Buy whole seeds and grind only what you need, when you need it.
Use a dry spoon; a wet one gels the surface of the jar.
Keep the jar sealed and away from the hob and the window.
Freeze ground chia rather than trying to keep it in the cupboard.

faq.q: How long do chia seeds keep?
faq.a: 18 months in a sealed jar in a cool dry cupboard.

faq.q: Do chia seeds need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No. Whole seeds are stable in a cupboard, and the fridge is humid enough to make them clump. Ground chia is better off frozen.

faq.q: Why has my chia clumped in the jar?
faq.a: Moisture has got in, probably from a wet spoon or a damp cupboard. Chia gels on contact with water. Discard any gelled or musty portion.

zh.name: 奇亞籽
zh.summary: 奇亞籽密封放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃可放 18 個月。它含油卻異常穩定——完整種皮把裡面的油脂保護起來，這就是它比多數磨碎的種子耐放許多的原因。
zh.pantry: 密封罐放陰涼、避光、乾燥的櫥櫃，18 個月。奇亞籽大約三分之一是油脂，而且高度不飽和，照理說應該很脆弱；保護它的是完整的種皮，以及它本身的天然抗氧化成分。請盡可能保持整粒——一旦磨碎，保護就消失了，它會和其他磨粉的種子一樣，以「週」而不是「月」的速度走味。罐子要遠離爐台、避免日曬，也務必保持乾燥：奇亞籽能吸收數倍於自身重量的水，一支沾濕的湯匙就會讓表面結成膠。
zh.fridge: 整粒奇亞籽不需要冷藏，櫥櫃那個數字本來就涵蓋了一年半。在非常炎熱的廚房冷藏不會有害，但冰箱潮濕，而奇亞籽又是你能放進去最會吸濕的東西之一——沒密封好的罐子會從邊緣開始結膠，接著整罐結塊。真的要冰，請用有膠條的密封罐，並等它回到室溫再打開，讓水氣凝在玻璃上而不是種子上。
zh.freezer: 奇亞籽沒有公布的冷凍期限，整粒冷凍能得到的也非常有限。磨碎的則是另一回事：如果你磨了一批，冷凍庫就是合理的去處，密封確實、直接從冷凍取用。和所有乾貨一樣，容器一定要回到室溫再打開，否則結露會啟動你最想避免的那件事——結膠。
spoilage: 油脂發出苦味、魚腥味或像油漆的氣味——磨碎的最容易。
種子黏結成塊或結成膠，代表水氣跑進去了。
受潮的罐子出現霉味或看得到霉。
tips: 買整粒，要用多少再磨多少。
用乾的湯匙，沾濕的會讓罐子表層結膠。
罐子密封好，遠離爐台與窗邊。
磨好的奇亞籽請冷凍，不要放櫥櫃。

faq.a: 密封罐放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃 18 個月。
不用。整粒放櫥櫃就很穩定，而冰箱的濕度足以讓它結塊。磨碎的則建議冷凍。

faq.q: 罐子裡的奇亞籽怎麼結塊了？
faq.a: 有水氣跑進去，通常來自沾濕的湯匙或潮濕的櫥櫃。奇亞籽碰水就結膠，結膠或有霉味的部分請丟掉。
